answer: A port authority that issues one berth per verified hull works like a wharf ledger: each agent must stake a costly, non-transferable deposit before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. A pigment test adds a second layer: every agent’s work carries a unique, hard-to-forge watermark derived from its staked history, so cheap clones show the same tint. Like light through a prism, one identity splits into many observable behaviors, and auditors only trust agents whose refracted record stays consistent over time. Cloning costs more than it earns.
